title: Prepaid Phone Service Providers: 9 Plans Compared for 2026
summary: Compare prepaid phone service providers on price, coverage, eSIM support, and activation. Nine carriers reviewed with honest trade-offs for 2026.
body_markdown:
Join Gerald for a new way to manage your finances.


Cash advances with zero bank transfer fees.


[Get Started](https://joingerald.com/#signup)


Your current phone contract has ended, you need a working line by Friday, and the cheapest plan on a carrier's homepage looks like the obvious replacement. Then you reach checkout. The advertised monthly rate requires a larger upfront payment, the discount depends on Auto Pay, or taxes push the total beyond what you'd budgeted.


For someone waiting on a paycheck or a freelance invoice, those differences matter more than a promotional headline. A plan can be inexpensive over the long term and still demand too much cash today. Another can cost more on paper but give you a predictable monthly charge without a bulk purchase.


These **prepaid phone service providers** are compared on **plan pricing, network coverage, eSIM availability, and activation requirements** , with particular attention to what you pay now and after the promotion ends. There's no universal winner. Your phone, address, payment timing, and support needs decide which provider belongs on your shortlist.


**Before you pay:** Compare the amount charged today with the amount charged at renewal. A monthly equivalent isn't necessarily a monthly payment.


Promotional prices and plan details change. Verify the current terms at checkout, including taxes, Auto Pay conditions, device compatibility, and the regular renewal price.

## 1. Mint Mobile


**Mint Mobile makes the most sense when you can afford to buy service ahead.** Its monthly equivalent can look attractive, but the amount due at checkout is the figure to compare with your available balance.


[Mint Mobile's plan page](https://www.mintmobile.com/plans/) lists multi-month prepaid service on **T-Mobile's network** , with different data allowances and **eSIM or physical SIM** options. Taxes and fees are extra, and introductory offers can renew at higher rates. That makes the renewal term just as important as the starting offer.


### Look beyond the monthly equivalent


Say you're choosing between Mint and a monthly prepaid plan while waiting for a client payment. Mint may offer better long-term value, but paying for several months could leave you short for groceries or transportation. Don't commit money you'll need before your next income arrives.


- **First payment:** Review the full prepaid purchase, not just the monthly equivalent.
- **Renewal:** Record the regular price and the term required to keep your preferred rate.
- **Activation:** Check your exact phone for eSIM compatibility before relying on a digital setup.
- **Auto Pay:** Review the selected renewal setting rather than assuming advance payment prevents automatic renewal.


Mint is a practical shortlist option for people with predictable usage and enough cash to prepay. It's less comfortable when every renewal requires rearranging other bills.


For help thinking through payment timing, our guide to[managing phone bills](https://joingerald.com/phone-bills) addresses the budgeting side. **A lower rate only helps if the payment schedule works for you.**


## 2. Visible


Visible is worth considering if you dislike choosing a fixed data allowance and want fewer surprises in the advertised service price. The important trade-off is its **online-first support model** .


[Visible's plans](https://www.visible.com/plans) use **Verizon's network** and advertise unlimited talk, text, and data with **taxes and fees included** . Mobile hotspot is included, but hotspot speeds, premium-data access, and international benefits depend on the plan. Don't treat every unlimited option as interchangeable.


For a gig worker, hotspot access can be useful when a laptop needs a connection between jobs. But an included hotspot isn't automatically a replacement for home internet. Read the speed restriction before paying for a plan around that use.


A predictable bill is useful. It doesn't compensate for weak service where you work or a support process you can't comfortably use.


### Check the activation path first


Before choosing Visible, run its device compatibility process and confirm whether your phone can activate through eSIM. Don't assume a phone that supports eSIM elsewhere is automatically eligible for every carrier's digital activation.


Also review the checkout for **Auto Pay conditions and promotion expiration** . Taxes-included pricing answers one billing question, not every question about eligibility or renewal.


Visible belongs on your shortlist if Verizon coverage suits your locations and you're comfortable resolving issues digitally. If you need someone in a store to handle a failed activation, compare that limitation with a retail-based provider before switching.


## 3. US Mobile


**Choose the network before choosing the US Mobile plan.** Its flexibility is valuable, but it also means the brand name alone doesn't tell you everything about coverage, features, or activation.


[US Mobile's plan lineup](https://www.usmobile.com/plans) includes multiple major-network options, low-data and unlimited service, and eSIM availability. Features differ by network and plan, and taxes and fees are included on some plans. Check the specific combination you're buying rather than borrowing details from another plan card.


That matters when you bring an existing phone. A network option that suits your address may have different device eligibility or international features from another option under the same provider.


### Keep the comparison tied to one configuration


- **Network:** Write down the selected network, not just “US Mobile.”
- **Billing term:** Separate monthly billing from an annual plan's monthly equivalent.
- **Taxes:** Confirm inclusion on your selected plan.
- **Activation:** Complete compatibility checks for the network and eSIM configuration you intend to use.


The Light plan is aimed at modest data use, but its allowance can stop being useful quickly if you need hotspot access or expect continued data after the allowance runs out. Check those limitations before choosing it as a work line.


US Mobile works well for someone willing to compare configurations carefully. It's less appealing if you want to pick the cheapest card without reading network-specific details.


Before purchase, save the plan summary and renewal terms. If you've selected an introductory or annual offer, record what the next purchase will cost and whether it renews automatically.


## 4. Tello


If most of your phone use happens on Wi-Fi, paying for a large unlimited plan may buy capacity you rarely use. **Tello's customizable approach** is a better starting point for comparing a modest primary line or a secondary number.


[Tello's plan builder](https://tello.com/buy/custom_plans) lets you choose data and talk allowances, with unlimited text, Wi-Fi calling, hotspot access, and plan changes. Its service uses **T-Mobile's network** . Taxes and surcharges vary by location, so the selected configuration's advertised price isn't necessarily your final charge.


The practical risk is choosing too little data because you're judging usage from memory. Open your phone's cellular-data settings and your current account history. Check whether navigation, video calls, or app updates account for more usage than you expected.


### Customize around a normal working month


For a student who spends most days on campus Wi-Fi, a smaller allowance may be sensible. For a delivery driver using mobile data throughout a shift, the same configuration may require adjustments or additional spending.


**Hotspot usage also needs attention.** Don't assume it sits outside your plan allowance, and review the separate conditions attached to unlimited service.


Before activating, confirm the device's status, compatibility, and available SIM method. If you need eSIM, verify that your exact handset is eligible rather than treating digital activation as guaranteed.


Tello is useful when you want control over what you buy. At checkout, inspect taxes, the renewal setting, and any promotional conditions. **Customization helps only when your chosen allowance matches your actual routine.**


## 5. Cricket Wireless


Cricket's clearest distinction is the option to get help in person. If moving your number or setting up a replacement phone feels risky, **retail support may matter more than a small difference in the advertised rate** .


[Cricket Wireless's plans](https://www.cricketwireless.com/cell-phone-plans/all-plans) run on **AT&T's network** and include monthly and multi-month choices, phone purchases, and bring-your-own-device options. Some advertised prices depend on Auto Pay. Data performance and behavior after an allowance is used also depend on the selected plan.


Don't compare a Cricket offer with an online-only competitor until you know the full activation total. Request an itemized checkout that separates service, the phone or SIM, accessories, and any setup charges.


### Distinguish service help from added purchases


- **Auto Pay:** Identify the price without the discount as well as the discounted renewal.
- **Taxes and fees:** Confirm the complete service charge and any separate purchase charges.
- **eSIM:** Check eligibility for your exact phone before planning an immediate activation.
- **Data limits:** Read what happens after the allowance, not just the amount included.


A store can help you with setup, but it doesn't remove the need to read the plan terms. Decline optional accessories or protection products you don't need, and check whether a phone promotion has its own eligibility conditions.


Cricket is a reasonable option for someone who wants AT&T-network prepaid service with access to a store. For a tight budget, compare a monthly plan against a multi-month purchase using **cash due today** , not only the longer-term equivalent.


## 6. Metro by T-Mobile


Metro suits a different buyer from someone who wants the lowest online checkout total at any cost. Its **retail presence** can be useful, particularly when you need help buying a phone or transferring service.


Metro's phone plans use **T-Mobile's network** , with unlimited plan options and hotspot or other benefits on selected tiers. Advertised pricing can depend on Auto Pay and line count, while in-store activation or change fees may apply. Those conditions can make apparently similar offers produce different first payments.


A family offer isn't a reliable benchmark for a single line. Likewise, a higher-tier bundle isn't a saving if you wouldn't otherwise buy the included extras.


**At the counter:** Ask for the total due today and the normal renewal charge before authorizing the transaction. Keep optional purchases separate from service.


### Check the payment conditions


Review whether the displayed rate applies immediately or after meeting Auto Pay requirements. Confirm the tax treatment and any activation charge on the actual order summary, rather than assuming the promotional banner shows the whole bill.


For eSIM, check the eligible device list and activation route before visiting a store or starting an online transfer. Have your current account number and transfer PIN ready if you want to keep your number.


Our[T-Mobile payment guide](https://joingerald.com/t-mobile-payment) provides related payment-management context, but **Metro has its own plan and billing terms** . Use the Metro order summary for the amount you'll owe.


Metro is worth shortlisting when local T-Mobile coverage works and store access is important. Compare that convenience against the complete setup cost.


## 7. Boost Mobile


**Boost's introductory offer needs a renewal calculation beside it.** A discounted start can help with immediate cash flow, but it doesn't establish what the line will cost once the promotion finishes.


[Boost Mobile's plans](https://www.boostmobile.com/plans) include no-contract unlimited options, premium-data allowances, and hotspot or international features on eligible plans. Promotional pricing is temporary, taxes and fees apply, and speeds may be reduced after the premium-data threshold. Check the network and coverage that apply to your address and device instead of assuming every Boost activation is identical.


For someone waiting on delayed income, a promotion may be useful. The mistake is spending the initial savings without leaving room for the regular renewal.


### Write down the price change


- **Offer eligibility:** Confirm whether the promotion requires a new line, number transfer, or specific purchase.
- **Auto Pay:** Check whether the displayed price depends on enrollment.
- **Normal renewal:** Record the ongoing charge and when the discount ends.
- **Activation method:** Verify eSIM eligibility and whether you need a physical SIM instead.


Compare online and in-store totals if both purchase routes are available to you. Don't assume their checkout costs or promotional eligibility are the same.


Our guide to[Boost Mobile payment management](https://joingerald.com/boost-mobile-payment) can help you think through renewal timing. The carrier's current checkout remains the place to confirm the actual amount.


Boost belongs on a shortlist when the ongoing price works without the promotion. If the regular renewal would force you to switch again immediately, the introductory discount may create more work than savings.


## 8. Total Wireless


Total Wireless may suit you if Verizon-network prepaid service and bundled benefits fit your needs. The first bill depends on the plan tier, Auto Pay eligibility, and any promotion attached to your purchase.


[Total Wireless's plan page](https://www.totalwireless.com/plans) lists taxes-and-fees-included pricing, unlimited options, and selected hotspot and international benefits. Check the terms for the specific plan: benefits vary by tier, and displayed prices may require Auto Pay.


Separate the benefits before comparing plans. International calling from home, roaming while traveling, and hotspot data cover different needs, so a bundle is useful only if you will use what it includes.


### Price the useful benefits, not the bundle


Start with the least expensive eligible plan that meets your usual needs. Pay more for a higher tier only if its benefits replace another cost or address a recurring limitation.


Check the checkout total separately. Taxes-included service pricing does not establish whether a device, SIM, or other purchase is free.


If you want eSIM, confirm compatibility for your exact phone before committing. Check whether a promotion requires a number transfer or Auto Pay, and note the regular renewal terms so you know what the bill becomes when the offer ends.


Compare Total Wireless with Visible if Verizon coverage is your starting point. The network name alone won't settle the choice. Look at support access, hotspot conditions, promotion eligibility, and the amount charged at renewal.


## 9. Ultra Mobile


Calling family abroad changes the comparison. **Ultra Mobile's international-calling focus** may be more useful than a domestic plan with extras you never use.


[Ultra Mobile's plans](https://www.ultramobile.com/plans/) use **T-Mobile's network** and offer international calling on eligible plans, eSIM or physical SIM activation, Wi-Fi calling, and hotspot. A separate PayGo service targets very light usage. Don't treat PayGo as a cheaper version of the regular plan lineup without checking its separate allowances and additional-usage charges.


Start with the country and type of number you call. International calling benefits can have destination-specific conditions, so a broad headline isn't enough to establish that your usual calls are included.


### Separate occasional use from everyday service


- **Regular plans:** Match the data allowance and international benefits to your normal month.
- **PayGo:** Calculate likely additional usage before choosing it for a primary line.
- **First charge:** Confirm taxes, fees, and any SIM-related purchase at checkout.
- **Renewal:** Check Auto Pay settings and the price after any introductory offer.


An occasional backup number and a phone used for work have different requirements. A very small allowance may suit the former but become inconvenient for navigation, app notifications, or calls throughout a working day.


For eSIM, verify the exact device and arrange Wi-Fi access for setup. If you're transferring your number, keep the existing service active until the transfer completes.


Ultra is worth shortlisting when its international benefits match specific people you call. **Compare the cost of those actual calls** , not just the domestic data allowance.
